## Context

PR #2185 (`paul/clone-et`, trail 1186) added `/et/<project>/<repo>` native clone refs and merged 2026-09-02T00:06Z. PR #2223 (`paul/clone-ref-findings`, commits 0083f834d + 55e69b893) then landed to address two review findings, and it fixed both correctly — dot-only `/gh/` refs keep the parser's reason, and `git@github.com:foo/bar` now says "pass GitHub mirrors as /gh/foo/bar". ## Item 1 (the main one): the `/et/`-prefixed form still loses its reason

`invalidCloneRefError` (repo_clone.go, added in 0083f834d) got a `mirrorCloneRefPrefixRe = ^/?gh/` branch that keeps the mirror parser's reason for malformed `gh/` refs. There is no symmetric `^/?et/` branch, so a native ref that fails the charset check falls through to the generic shape list. Verified against a binary built from ee6d53f3d:

    /et/foo_bar/dogbark  ->  invalid <repo> "/et/foo_bar/dogbark": expected /et/<project>/<repo>, <project>/<repo>, /gh/<owner>/<repo>, or a full entire:// URL
    /et/paul/dog_bark    ->  (identical)
    /et/paul/            ->  (identical)

The user typed exactly `/et/<project>/<repo>` and is told to type `/et/<project>/<repo>`. That is the same self-contradiction #2223 set out to remove, reproduced on the other side. Add an `^/?et/` branch that names the actual rule, mirroring what `parseMirrorCloneRef` now does for owner/repo ("project: lowercase letters, digits, '-'; repo: also interior '.'"). Note the existing `gh/` branch produces the ref twice in one message (`invalid <repo> "/gh/entirehq/..": repo cannot be dot-only: /gh/entirehq/..`) — worth not copying that shape.

## Item 2: the native charsets are looser than the server's, and the doc comment misstates the rules

I read the authoritative source in ~/Work/entire/devenv/entiredb at 2b81a3557 — `core/resource/project_name.go`, function `normalizeName`, reached from `core/coreapi/repos.go:75` (the repo-create path the CLI hits) and `core/api/admin_handlers.go:1381`. The real rules:

| rule | project | repo |
|---|---|---|
| charset | lowercase a-z, 0-9, `-` | same plus interior `.` |
| length | 3–32 | 1–64 |
| leading/trailing `-` | banned | banned |
| leading/trailing `.` | n/a | banned |
| consecutive `..` | n/a | banned |
| raw ULID as a name | banned | banned |
| uppercase | rejected at create; `foldProjectName` lowercases for lookup | same |

Against the CLI's `nativeProjectRe = ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$` and `nativeRepoRe = ^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$`, three things are wrong in the permissive direction, so refs the server can never match become a control-plane round trip instead of a local shape error: leading/trailing `-`, leading/trailing `.`, and consecutive dots. `paul/..`, `paul/.foo`, `paul/foo.`, `paul/-x` all currently parse as native refs. The mirror side already has `gitHubDotOnlyRe` for exactly this class; the native side has no equivalent. - "3–32 chars server-side" for projects is right (`projectNameMinLen`/`projectNameMaxLen`), so the `gh`/`et` two-char guard is genuinely safe. They are not in `reserved_names.txt`; the length rule is what excludes them.
- Accepting uppercase in the CLI regex is right, because lookups fold case.
- `resolveRepoRef`'s ULID short-circuit is safe, because `LooksLikeRawULID` (core/model/id.go:28) is banned as a name at create time, so a 26-char Crockford string in the ref position is always an ID.

## Verification

Existing tests to extend: `TestParseNativeCloneRef` and `TestInvalidCloneRefError` in `cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone_test.go`. There is currently no case covering an `/et/`-prefixed ref that fails the charset check — that gap is why item 1 shipped. Add the dot/hyphen edge cases too.

Repo standard before commit is `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci`; treat fmt-then-lint as one sequence. On main today the clone tests pass and `mise run lint` reports 0 issues, so anything failing is yours. Two known-unrelated local failures on macOS: `TestCodexAppServerHooksList_*` (`/var` vs `/private/var`) and versioncheck tests misclassifying `/usr/local` as Homebrew.

Please reference trail 1186 and PR #2185/#2223 in the PR body so the lineage is traceable, and note in the body that item 2 tightens client-side validation against rules verified in entiredb `core/resource/project_name.go` rather than inferred. Repo convention: never hard-wrap prose in PR bodies, one paragraph per line.
</cross-session-message>

65	// nativeProjectRe / nativeRepoRe are the server's project- and repo-name
66	// charsets (entiredb core/resource/project_name.go: letters, digits, '-', plus
67	// '.' for repos; lookups fold case, so uppercase is accepted here). Length and
68	// edge-character rules are left to the server — this check only has to tell a
69	// native ref apart from things that are not one.
70	var (
71		nativeProjectRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$`)
72		nativeRepoRe    = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$`)
73	)
74	
75	// parseNativeCloneRef turns a native clone ref — `/et/<project>/<repo>` or the
76	// `<project>/<repo>` shorthand, leading slash optional — into its project and
77	// repo names. Not a match (ok == false) is not an error: the caller falls
78	// through to the mirror grammar. The `gh`/`et` forge tokens are never valid
79	// project names (3–32 chars server-side), so a two-segment ref starting with
80	// one is a malformed forge ref, not a shorthand, and is rejected here so the
81	// mirror parser can name the expected shape. Segments must match the server's
82	// name charsets: without that, any "x/y" — `git@github.com:foo/bar` included —
83	// parsed as a shorthand and produced a control-plane lookup error instead of a
84	// hint about the accepted shapes.
85	func parseNativeCloneRef(ref string) (project, repo string, ok bool) {
86		segs := strings.Split(strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(ref), "/"), "/")
87		if len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] == nativeCloneForge {
88			segs = segs[1:]
89		}
90		if len(segs) != 2 || !nativeProjectRe.MatchString(segs[0]) || !nativeRepoRe.MatchString(segs[1]) {
91			return "", "", false
92		}
93		if segs[0] == nativeCloneForge || segs[0] == "gh" {
94			return "", "", false
95		}
96		return segs[0], segs[1], true
97	}
98	
99	// resolveNativeCloneURL resolves an Entire-native repo (by project and repo
100	// name) to its entire:// clone URL: name → ULID via the project-scoped lookup,
101	// then GetRepo — the one call that returns both clusterHost and path. The URL
102	// is the server's own coordinates via repoRemoteURL, never synthesized from
103	// the user's ref (note: no .git suffix — the server strips it for /gh/ paths
104	// only, so a /et/ path with it would 404).
105	func resolveNativeCloneURL(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client, project, repoName string) (string, error) {
106		repoID, err := resolveRepoRef(ctx, c, repoName, project)
107		if err != nil {
108			return "", err
109		}
110		repo, err := c.GetRepo(ctx, coreapi.GetRepoParams{RepoId: repoID})
111		if err != nil {
112			return "", fmt.Errorf("get repo: %w", err)
113		}
114		cloneURL := repoRemoteURL(*repo)
115		if cloneURL == "" {
116			return "", fmt.Errorf("repo %s/%s has no clone URL yet (still provisioning?)", project, repoName)
117		}
118		// The host is server-provided but interpolated into the entire:// clone URL,
119		// so apply the same anti-token-leak guard as the mirror path (see the
120		// validateClusterHost call on the /gh/ branch).
121		if err := validateClusterHost(repo.ClusterHost.Or("")); err != nil {
122			return "", fmt.Errorf("repo has an invalid cluster host %q: %w", repo.ClusterHost.Or(""), err)
123		}
124		return cloneURL, nil
125	}
126	
127	// mirrorCloneRefPrefixRe matches the `gh/` forge token (leading slash optional)
128	// that says the user meant a mirror ref, so a malformed one gets an error about
129	// its owner/repo rather than a list of every shape `repo clone` accepts.
130	var mirrorCloneRefPrefixRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^/?gh/`)
131	
132	// cloneRefShapes lists every ref shape `repo clone` accepts, for error text.
133	const cloneRefShapes = "/et/<project>/<repo>, <project>/<repo>, /gh/<owner>/<repo>, or a full entire:// URL"
134	
135	// invalidCloneRefError explains why ref matched none of the clone grammars.
136	// A GitHub URL gets pointed at the `/gh/` form it should have been; a `gh/`
137	// ref that the mirror parser rejected keeps the parser's reason (bad owner or
138	// repo charset, dot-only repo, missing segment), and anything else gets the
139	// list of accepted shapes.
140	func invalidCloneRefError(ref string, mirrorErr error) error {
141		// Hosted forms only: bare `x/y` is what the native shorthand already
142		// rejected, and a truncated `gh/foo` would otherwise read as owner "gh".
143		// The parser's dot-only guard also keeps `foo/..` out of the hint.
144		if owner, repo, err := parseHostedGitHubURL(ref); err == nil {
145			return fmt.Errorf("invalid <repo> %q: pass GitHub mirrors as /gh/%s/%s", ref, owner, repo)
146		}
147		if mirrorCloneRefPrefixRe.MatchString(ref) {
148			return fmt.Errorf("invalid <repo> %q: %w", ref, mirrorErr)
149		}
150		return fmt.Errorf("invalid <repo> %q: expected %s", ref, cloneRefShapes)
151	}
152	
153	// parseMirrorCloneRef turns a clone ref like `/gh/entirehq/entire-api` into the
154	// API provider ("github") and the lowercased owner/repo. The `gh` token is the
155	// path provider used in entire:// clone URLs; it maps to the "github" upstream
156	// provider the control plane records.
157	func parseMirrorCloneRef(ref string) (provider, owner, repo string, err error) {
158		m := mirrorCloneRefRe.FindStringSubmatch(strings.TrimSpace(ref))
159		if m == nil {
160			return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("expected gh/<owner>/<repo> (leading slash optional; owner: letters, digits, '-'; repo: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'), got %q", ref)
161		}
162		owner, repo = strings.ToLower(m[1]), strings.ToLower(m[2])
163		if gitHubDotOnlyRe.MatchString(repo) {
164			return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("repo cannot be dot-only: %s", ref)
165		}
166		return mirrorCloneProviderGitHub, owner, repo, nil
167	}
168	
169	func newRepoCloneCmd() *cobra.Command {
170		var cluster string
171		cmd := &cobra.Command{
172			Use:   "clone <repo> [target-dir]",
173			Short: "Clone an Entire repository",
174			Long: "Clone an Entire-native repo by its `/et/<project>/<repo>` ref (or the " +
175				"`<project>/<repo>` shorthand), a GitHub mirror by its `/gh/<owner>/<repo>` " +
176				"ref, or a full `entire://` clone URL.\n\n" +
177				"A native ref resolves the repo's home cluster and clones from there " +
178				"(--cluster doesn't apply).\n\n" +
179				"With a `/gh/<owner>/<repo>` ref, looks up where the repo is mirrored: if " +
180				"it's on a single cluster, clones it directly; if it's mirrored on more " +
181				"than one, prompts you to pick which to clone from (or pass --cluster to " +
182				"choose non-interactively).\n\n" +
183				"A full `entire://` URL already names the cluster, so it's passed straight " +
184				"through to `git clone` with no lookup (and --cluster is ignored). The " +
185				"optional [target-dir] is passed through to `git clone` either way.",
186			Example: "  entire repo clone /et/project/example\n" +
187				"  entire repo clone project/example\n" +
188				"  entire repo clone /gh/entirehq/entire-api\n" +
189				"  entire repo clone /gh/entirehq/entire-api ./entire-api\n" +
190				"  entire repo clone /gh/entirehq/entire-api --cluster aws-us-east-2.entire.io\n" +
191				"  entire repo clone entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire-api",
192			Args: cobra.RangeArgs(1, 2),
193			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
194				cmd.SilenceUsage = true
195				// Trim once up front so the entire:// detection and the value forwarded
196				// to git clone agree (the shorthand path trims inside parseMirrorCloneRef).
197				ref := strings.TrimSpace(args[0])
198				var targetDir string
199				if len(args) > 1 {
200					targetDir = args[1]
201				}
202	
203				// A full entire:// clone URL already embeds the cluster host (it's what
204				// --cluster would otherwise resolve to), so pass it verbatim to git clone
205				// — no mirror lookup or cluster resolution. --cluster is irrelevant here.
206				//
207				// Deliberately NOT run through validateClusterHost: this is a raw URL the
208				// user typed, forwarded to `git clone` exactly as given (the whole point
209				// of this branch), so it's equivalent to running `git clone entire://…`
210				// directly. The validateClusterHost guard applies on the shorthand path
211				// where we *synthesize* the URL from a --cluster flag or an API-supplied
212				// host — values that flow into the STS audience under our own construction.
213				if isEntireCloneURL(ref) {
214					return runGitClone(cmd.Context(), cmd, ref, targetDir)
215				}
216	
217				// Native ref: resolve the repo's home cluster via the active-context
218				// control plane and clone from there. A native repo lives on exactly
219				// one home cluster, so --cluster has nothing to choose between.
220				if project, repoName, ok := parseNativeCloneRef(ref); ok {
221					if cluster != "" {
222						return fmt.Errorf("--cluster applies to /gh/ mirror refs; %s/%s is cloned from its home cluster", project, repoName)
223					}
224					var cloneURL string
225					if err := runCore(cmd, func(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client) error {
226						url, err := resolveNativeCloneURL(ctx, c, project, repoName)
227						if err != nil {
228							return err
229						}
230						cloneURL = url
231						return nil
232					}); err != nil {
233						return err
234					}
235					return runGitClone(cmd.Context(), cmd, cloneURL, targetDir)
236				}
237	
238				// provider is always "github" for the /gh/ shorthand; the pull-gated
239				// resolver pins the provider itself, so it's not threaded through.
240				_, owner, repo, err := parseMirrorCloneRef(ref)
241				if err != nil {
242					return invalidCloneRefError(ref, err)
243				}
244	
245				var placements []coreapi.ResolvedPlacement
246				lister := func(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client) error {
247					ps, err := resolvePullablePlacements(ctx, c, owner, repo)
248					if err != nil {
249						return err
250					}
251					placements = ps
252					return nil
253				}
254				// An explicit --cluster may name a cluster in a different federation
255				// than the active context, whose mirrors the active-context core can't
256				// see (the original bug: cloning a royalcanin.partial.to mirror while a
257				// different context is active failed with "not mirrored on ..."). Dial
258				// the core fronting that cluster — discovered from its well-known and
259				// authenticated with the matching local context, the same path
260				// `mirror create <url> [cluster]` uses — so the lookup resolves against
261				// the right federation. With no --cluster, list from the active context.
262				runWithCore := runCore
263				if cluster != "" {
264					if err := validateClusterHost(cluster); err != nil {
265						return fmt.Errorf("invalid --cluster: %w", err)
266					}
267					runWithCore = func(cmd *cobra.Command, fn func(context.Context, *coreapi.Client) error) error {
268						return runCoreForCluster(cmd, cluster, fn)
269					}
270				}
271				if err := runWithCore(cmd, lister); err != nil {
272					return err
273				}
274	
275				if len(placements) == 0 {
276					return fmt.Errorf("no mirror found for /gh/%s/%s; run 'entire repo mirror create github.com/%s/%s' to onboard it", owner, repo, owner, repo)
277				}
278	
279				chosen, err := selectCloneTarget(cmd, placements, cluster)
280				if err != nil {
281					return err
282				}
283	
284				// chosen.ClusterHost is server-provided, but it's interpolated into the
285				// entire:// clone URL just like the user-supplied --cluster, so apply the
286				// same anti-token-leak guard (validateClusterHost) before building it —
287				// defense-in-depth against a malformed host reaching git / the STS audience.
288				if err := validateClusterHost(chosen.ClusterHost); err != nil {
289					return fmt.Errorf("mirror has an invalid cluster host %q: %w", chosen.ClusterHost, err)
290				}
291				cloneURL := mirrorCloneURL(chosen.ClusterHost, owner, repo)
292				return runGitClone(cmd.Context(), cmd, cloneURL, targetDir)
293			},
294		}
295		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&cluster, "cluster", "", "Cluster host to clone from when the repo is mirrored on more than one (may belong to another auth context)")
296		return cmd
297	}
298	
299	// mirrorLister is the subset of the control-plane client listMirrorsForRepo
300	// needs. Narrowing to an interface lets callers (e.g. resolveCurrentRepoID in
301	// api_cmd.go, and entireapi_client.go's currentRepoRef) inject a fake control
302	// plane in tests; *coreapi.Client satisfies it.
303	type mirrorLister interface {
304		ListMirrors(ctx context.Context, params coreapi.ListMirrorsParams) (*coreapi.ListMirrorsOutputBody, error)
305	}
306	
307	// listMirrorsForRepo returns every mirror placement of one upstream repo across
308	// clusters. The list API filters by provider+owner server-side but has no repo
309	// filter, so the repo match is applied client-side (owner is already lowercased
310	// to match what the server persists).
311	func listMirrorsForRepo(ctx context.Context, c mirrorLister, provider, owner, repo string) ([]coreapi.Mirror, error) {
312		all, err := fetchAllPages(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, cursor string) ([]coreapi.Mirror, string, error) {
313			params := coreapi.ListMirrorsParams{
314				Provider: coreapi.NewOptString(provider),
315				Owner:    coreapi.NewOptString(owner),
316			}
317			if cursor != "" {
318				params.PageToken = coreapi.NewOptString(cursor)
319			}
320			out, err := c.ListMirrors(ctx, params)
321			if err != nil {
322				return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("list mirrors: %w", err)
323			}
324			return out.Mirrors, out.NextPageToken.Or(""), nil
325		})
326		if err != nil {
327			return nil, err
328		}
329		matched := make([]coreapi.Mirror, 0, len(all))
330		for _, m := range all {
331			if strings.EqualFold(m.Repo, repo) {
332				matched = append(matched, m)
333			}
334		}
335		return matched, nil
336	}
337	
338	// resolvePullablePlacements returns every cluster placement of one GitHub
339	// upstream the caller may pull (clone). It backs `repo clone /gh/<owner>/<repo>`
340	// and deliberately differs from listMirrorsForRepo: that reads the
341	// affiliation-scoped mirror list (repo#list), which omits public mirrors the
342	// caller holds no grant on, so the shorthand used to fail on a public repo that
343	// clones fine by full entire:// URL. This hits the pull-gated /mirrors/placements
344	// endpoint instead — the same authority the clone's STS exchange enforces — so
345	// anything clonable resolves, public or private-with-grant.
346	//
347	// owner/repo arrive already lowercased from parseMirrorCloneRef; the server
348	// matches case-insensitively regardless. An empty result means not mirrored or
349	// not pullable, and the caller surfaces that.
350	func resolvePullablePlacements(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client, owner, repo string) ([]coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, error) {
351		out, err := c.ResolveMirrorPlacements(ctx, coreapi.ResolveMirrorPlacementsParams{
352			Provider: coreapi.ResolveMirrorPlacementsProviderGithub,
353			Owner:    owner,
354			Repo:     repo,
355		})
356		if err != nil {
357			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve mirror placements: %w", err)
358		}
359		return out.Placements, nil
360	}
361	
362	// placementPicker adapts selectPlacement's messages to the calling verb. The
363	// picker logic is identical for every consumer (dedupe by host, honor an
364	// explicit selector, prompt only when there's a real choice); only the words
365	// differ, so they're passed in rather than duplicated per command.
366	type placementPicker struct {
367		// selector names the non-interactive way to choose a cluster, as the user
368		// would type it (e.g. `--cluster`). Interpolated into the no-terminal error
369		// so the pointer names a flag the calling command actually accepts.
370		selector string
371		// title is the interactive single-select's prompt.
372		title string
373		// action names the operation in the cancellation message, capitalized
374		// ("Clone", "Remote update") — handleFormCancellation prints
375		// "<action> cancelled."
376		action string
377	}
378	
379	// selectCloneTarget resolves which mirror placement to clone from, with the
380	// clone verb's wording. See selectPlacement for the selection rules.
381	func selectCloneTarget(cmd *cobra.Command, placements []coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, clusterFlag string) (coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, error) {
382		return selectPlacement(cmd, placements, clusterFlag, placementPicker{
383			selector: "--cluster",
384			title:    "This repo is mirrored on more than one cluster — pick one to clone from",
385			action:   "Clone",
386		})
387	}
388	
389	// selectPlacement resolves which mirror placement a verb should act on. With one
390	// placement it returns it directly. With an explicit clusterSel it picks the
391	// matching one (or errors listing the available hosts). With more than one and no
392	// selector it prompts interactively, failing fast with a p.selector pointer when
393	// there's no terminal.
394	func selectPlacement(cmd *cobra.Command, placements []coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, clusterSel string, p placementPicker) (coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, error) {
395		// Dedupe by cluster host: one placement per cluster is what a caller acts on,
396		// and the same host appearing twice would only confuse the picker. Key on the
397		// case-folded host — DNS is case-insensitive, so a selector value differing
398		// only in case from the API's ClusterHost must still match (the alternative is
399		// a misleading "not mirrored on ..." after a successful lookup + dial).
400		byHost := make(map[string]coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, len(placements))
401		hosts := make([]string, 0, len(placements))
402		for _, p := range placements {
403			key := strings.ToLower(p.ClusterHost)
404			if _, seen := byHost[key]; seen {
405				continue
406			}
407			byHost[key] = p
408			hosts = append(hosts, key)
409		}
410		sort.Strings(hosts)
411	
412		if clusterSel != "" {
413			match, ok := byHost[strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(clusterSel))]
414			if !ok {
415				return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, fmt.Errorf("repo is not mirrored on %q; available: %s", clusterSel, strings.Join(hosts, ", "))
416			}
417			return match, nil
418		}
419	
420		if len(hosts) == 1 {
421			return byHost[hosts[0]], nil
422		}
423	
424		if !interactive.CanPromptInteractively() {
425			return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, fmt.Errorf("repo is mirrored on %d clusters; pass %s to choose one of: %s", len(hosts), p.selector, strings.Join(hosts, ", "))
426		}
427	
428		options := make([]huh.Option[string], len(hosts))
429		for i, h := range hosts {
430			options[i] = huh.NewOption(mirrorCellLabel(byHost[h]), h)
431		}
432		var selected string
433		form := NewAccessibleForm(
434			huh.NewGroup(
435				huh.NewSelect[string]().
436					Title(p.title).
437					Options(options...).
438					Value(&selected),
439			),
440		)
441		if err := form.RunWithContext(cmd.Context()); err != nil {
442			// handleFormCancellation prints "<action> cancelled." and returns nil for a
443			// Ctrl+C / cancelled-context abort. Surface that as a SilentError so the
444			// caller stops instead of falling through to act on a zero-value target
445			// (the `entire:///gh/...` empty-host bug) without main.go reprinting the
446			// message handleFormCancellation already wrote; a real form error propagates.
447			if cerr := handleFormCancellation(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), p.action, err); cerr != nil {
448				return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, cerr
449			}
450			return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, NewSilentError(fmt.Errorf("%s cancelled", strings.ToLower(p.action)))
451		}
452		match, ok := byHost[selected]
453		if !ok {
454			// The form succeeded but handed back a host that is not on offer. Nothing
455			// has been printed here, so this must NOT be a SilentError — main.go
456			// suppresses those, and the command would exit non-zero with no message.
457			return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, fmt.Errorf("no cluster selected from the %d offered", len(hosts))
458		}
459		return match, nil
460	}
461	
462	// mirrorCellLabel is the human label for a mirror placement in the clone picker:
463	// the physical cell and jurisdiction when known, always anchored by the cluster
464	// host that goes into the clone URL.
465	func mirrorCellLabel(p coreapi.ResolvedPlacement) string {
466		cell := strings.TrimSpace(p.Cell.Or(""))
467		jur := strings.TrimSpace(p.Jurisdiction.Or(""))
468		switch {
469		case cell != "" && jur != "":
470			return fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s) — %s", cell, jur, p.ClusterHost)
471		case cell != "":
472			return fmt.Sprintf("%s — %s", cell, p.ClusterHost)
473		default:
474			return p.ClusterHost
475		}
476	}
477	
478	// runGitClone shells out to `git clone <cloneURL> [target-dir]`, wiring the
479	// child's stdio through so git-remote-entire's auth prompts and clone progress
480	// reach the user. A clone failure is wrapped as a SilentError: git already
481	// printed its own diagnostics, so main.go shouldn't reprint the wrapper.
482	func runGitClone(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, cloneURL, targetDir string) error {
483		args := []string{"clone", cloneURL}
484		if targetDir != "" {
485			args = append(args, targetDir)
486		}
487		fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Cloning %s\n", cloneURL)
488		gitCmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", args...)
489		gitCmd.Stdin = cmd.InOrStdin()
490		gitCmd.Stdout = cmd.OutOrStdout()
491		gitCmd.Stderr = cmd.ErrOrStderr()
492		if err := gitCmd.Run(); err != nil {
493			return NewSilentError(fmt.Errorf("git clone failed: %w", err))
494		}
495		return nil
496	}

Examples:

  Context: The user has just implemented a new component based on a Figma design.
  user: "I've finished implementing the hero section based on the Figma design"
  assistant: "I'll review how well your implementation matches the Figma design."

  Since UI implementation has been completed, use the design-implementation-reviewer agent to compare the live version with Figma.

  </example>

- entire-engineering:design:design-iterator: Use this agent PROACTIVELY when design work isn't coming together on the first attempt. ## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## plugin:datadog:mcp
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## plugin:entire-engineering:context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

- slack:slack-api: Discover, navigate, and call Slack Web API methods (the family.method endpoints at slack.com/api like chat.postMessage, conversations.history, users.info, views.open). Use this skill whenever the developer asks which Slack API method does something, needs a method's required OAuth scopes or token type, wants to call or test a Web API method, is handling cursor pagination (next_cursor), hitting rate limits (tier/ratelimited/Retry-After), or debugging API errors like missing_scope, invalid_auth, or channel_not_found. Also trigger when they paste a slack.com/api/ URL or a docs.slack.dev/reference/methods link, or ask how to list/fetch/post/update Slack resources via the API. This skill covers the Web API method layer: finding the right method, reading its contract (scopes, arguments, errors), and calling it over raw HTTP with curl or through a Slack SDK.
- slack:slack-cli: Use the Slack CLI to create, run, and manage Slack apps from the terminal. Use whenever the developer wants to log in, add a team, switch workspaces, or authenticate with Slack; whenever Slack CLI commands are needed (local development with `slack run`, managing app lifecycle, the manifest).
- slack:slack-docs: Search and read the official Slack platform documentation at docs.slack.dev. Use this skill to answer conceptual or how-to questions about Slack features. You can also use it to look up, fetch, or summarize specific guide pages from provided docs.slack.dev links.
- slack:slack-messaging: Compose and format effective Slack messages sent via the Slack MCP tools. Use whenever writing, drafting, scheduling, or improving a Slack message, announcement, or reply. Covers standard markdown formatting, message structure, thread etiquette, reactions, and scheduling, and points to the right dialect for canvases and Block Kit.
- slack:slack-search: Find messages, files, channels, and people across Slack with the search MCP tools. Use whenever locating conversations, gathering context before answering, or looking someone up. Covers search modifiers, file-type filters, natural-language vs. keyword search, and reading results in context.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. - `project`: control-plane project management — `create`, `list`, `get`, `delete`
- `repo`: control-plane repository lifecycle — `create`, `list`, `get`, `delete`,
  `clone`, plus the `mirror` and `visibility` subtrees. Git content operations
  (log, diff, …) are intentionally out of scope. The `mirror` subtree is
  server-side (`create`, `list`, `get`, `remove`, `collaborators`) with one
  exception: `mirror use` repoints the *current clone's* git remote at a mirror
  (local git config only — it creates nothing server-side). Interactively it
  picks among the repo's placements and asks whether to replace the remote
  (preserving the old URL under `--upstream`) or add a separate one;
  non-interactively it repoints `--remote` directly. Both `use` and `clone`
  choose a placement through the shared `selectPlacement` picker. `clone`
  accepts a native `/et/<project>/<repo>` ref (or the `<project>/<repo>`
  shorthand — the `gh`/`et` forge tokens can never be project names, which are
  3+ chars server-side, so the grammar is unambiguous; both segments must also
  match the server's name charsets, so `git@github.com:foo/bar` is not a
  shorthand), a mirror `/gh/<owner>/<repo>` ref, or a full `entire://` URL
  passed through verbatim. A ref matching none of these gets a targeted error
  (`invalidCloneRefError`): a GitHub URL is pointed at its `/gh/` form, a
  malformed `gh/` ref keeps the mirror parser's reason, anything else lists
  the accepted shapes.
  A native ref resolves project → repo ULID → `GetRepo`, whose response is the
  only one carrying both `clusterHost` and `path`, and clones
  `entire://<clusterHost><path>` from the repo's home cluster (no `.git`
  suffix — the server strips it for `/gh/` paths only; `--cluster` is
  rejected on native refs).
- `grant`: manage access grants and org membership — `org`, `project`, and `repo`
  each support `add` / `list` / `remove`

input.command:
cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-soph--herdr-worktrees-cli-soph-repo-clone-followup/5d677c01-0e73-474c-ac40-4fd2c9a54c33/scratchpad/pr_body.md <<'EOF'
Follow-up to #2185 (native `/et/<project>/<repo>` clone refs, trail 1186) and #2223 (its first round of review findings). #2223's two fixes are correct and untouched here: a dot-only `/gh/` ref keeps the mirror parser's reason, and `git@github.com:foo/bar` is pointed at `/gh/foo/bar`. This is what it left behind.

## 1. An `/et/`-prefixed ref lost its reason

#2223 gave `invalidCloneRefError` a `^/?gh/` branch so a malformed mirror ref keeps the mirror parser's reason. There was no symmetric `^/?et/` branch, so a native ref that failed the charset check fell through to the generic shape list:

```
$ entire repo clone /et/foo_bar/dogbark
invalid <repo> "/et/foo_bar/dogbark": expected /et/<project>/<repo>, <project>/<repo>, /gh/<owner>/<repo>, or a full entire:// URL
```

The user typed exactly `/et/<project>/<repo>` and was told to type `/et/<project>/<repo>` — the same self-contradiction #2223 set out to remove, reproduced on the other side. `parseNativeCloneRef` now returns an error rather than a bool, `invalidCloneRefError` grows the `et/` branch, and the message names the rule that was broken:

```
invalid <repo> "/et/foo_bar/dogbark": project "foo_bar" must be 3-32 characters of letters, digits and '-', not starting or ending with '-'
invalid <repo> "/et/paul/dog_bark":   repo "dog_bark" must be 1-64 characters of letters, digits, '.' and '-', not starting or ending with '.' or '-', and with no consecutive dots
invalid <repo> "/et/paul":            expected /et/<project>/<repo> or <project>/<repo> (2 names, got 1)
```

Declaring a forge token is the whole test for showing a parser's reason. A bare two-segment ref (`paul/.foo`) still gets the shape list, deliberately: it declared nothing, so it is equally a mangled URL — `git@github.com:foo/bar` is itself just a bad "project" name under the shorthand grammar, which is exactly the case #2223 fixed. That boundary is now pinned by a test.

The reasons name the offending segment rather than repeating the whole ref, so they avoid the shape the `gh/` branch produces (`invalid <repo> "/gh/entirehq/..": repo cannot be dot-only: /gh/entirehq/..`). The `gh/` messages are unchanged.

## 2. The native name check was looser than the server

The client accepted `^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$` / `^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$` and left everything else to the server, so `paul/..`, `paul/.foo`, `paul/foo.` and `paul/-x` all parsed as native refs and cost a control-plane round trip to be told the repo does not exist. This tightens both regexes to the shape the server actually enforces, verified in entiredb `core/resource/project_name.go` (`normalizeName`, reached from `core/coreapi/repos.go:75` — the repo-create path the CLI hits — and `core/api/admin_handlers.go:1381`) rather than inferred: projects are 3–32 chars of lowercase letters, digits and `-`; repos 1–64 with interior `.` also allowed; neither may start or end with `-` (or `.`); no consecutive dots; and a raw ULID is refused as a name.

Three things the old comment got right and this keeps. Uppercase is still accepted, because both lookups fold case — the project through `foldProjectName`, and the repo on `lower(repo_registry.name)` in `getRepoGroupByProjectAndFullName`. The 3-char project minimum is real (`projectNameMinLen`), which is what makes the `<project>/<repo>` shorthand unambiguous; encoding it directly replaces the hand-written `gh`/`et` forge-token guard with the rule that guard was standing in for, so `ab/dogbark` is now a local shape error too. And the `..`/edge-dot bans are the reason `entire-trails.el` stays legal while `paul/..` does not.

Consecutive dots are checked outside the regex because RE2 has no negative lookahead. Interior hyphen runs and a hyphen adjacent to a dot (`dog--bark`, `dog-.bark`) are names the server accepts, so they are pinned as accepted — a per-segment regex, the tempting simplification here, would refuse them.

## 3. A `.git` suffix on a native ref

`entire repo clone /et/paul/dogbark.git` parsed and then failed at lookup with `no repo named "dogbark.git" in that project` and no hint, even though the server strips `.git` for `/gh/` paths only.

It is deliberately not stripped or refused at parse time: `foo.git` is a legal server repo name under the rules above (interior dot, no trailing dot, no `..`) — the same shape as `entire-trails.el`, and indistinguishable from it in the ref — so stripping could clone a different repo than the one named. The advice is attached at the lookup miss instead, the first point where the suffix is provably the cause. `noRepoNamedErr` becomes a typed error so the clone path can recognise the miss with `errors.As` instead of matching its text; its message is unchanged.

```
no repo named "dogbark.git" in that project (run `entire repo list <project>` to see names, or pass a ULID); a native ref keeps the .git suffix (it is stripped for /gh/ paths only) — retry as /et/paul/dogbark
```

The full-`entire://`-URL branch performs no lookup of ours, so it gets the same advice as a hedged note on stderr after `git clone` fails, and only for an `/et/` path carrying the suffix — a failed clone is just as likely to be auth or the network, and git has already printed the real diagnosis above it.

## Two corrections to earlier claims about the server rules

The name constraints **are** part of the contract, and my earlier note saying they "aren't in the contract" was wrong on both of its grounds. `internal/coreapi/spec/core.openapi.json` having `CreateProjectInputBody.name` as minLength 1 / maxLength 100 with no pattern only describes the wire shape; the resource layer enforces the real rules underneath it. And `gh:mirrors:01KS00CRNX8HFG5PX19S2WH2F0` is not a counter-example: it is a deliberate system-namespace project (`MirrorsProjectNamePrefix`, `core/resource/store.go:1458`) that `CreateProject` refuses to mint because of the `:`, looked up through `findProjectByExactName`, which skips the shape check on purpose.

Pinning the resource-layer rules into the OpenAPI schema is still worth doing, so the generated client is not built against a looser contract than the server enforces — but it belongs in entiredb, not here: `core.openapi.json` is the pristine upstream spec, refreshed by curl-ing the running server (see `internal/coreapi/gen.go`), so a hand edit in this repo would be reverted by the next sync.

## One thing left open, out of scope

`resolveRepoRef`'s ULID short-circuit is safe in practice but not for quite the stated reason. The CLI's `looksLikeULID` accepts any 26 Crockford-base32 characters, while the server's `LooksLikeRawULID` (`core/model/id.go:28`) additionally requires the first character to be in `0`-`7`. A name like `REDACTED` is therefore a legal server repo name that the CLI misreads as an ID (verified against both predicates). Tightening `looksLikeULID` to match would be a one-line change and cannot reject a real ULID, but it is shared by every org/project/repo/grant ref, so it is a decision for its own PR rather than a clone-parsing follow-up.

## Verification

`mise run fmt && mise run lint` clean, `mise run test:ci` green. `TestParseNativeCloneRef` and `TestInvalidCloneRefError` are extended with the `/et/`-prefixed and dot/hyphen/length edge cases that were missing — the absence of any case for an `/et/` ref failing the charset check is why item 1 shipped — plus new tests for the `.git` hint on a lookup miss, its restriction to that miss, and the passthrough note.

content.text:
Done — **PR #2240** against `main`: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2240

All three items landed in `cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go` (plus a typed error in `resolveref.go`):

**Item 1 — the `/et/` reason.** `parseNativeCloneRef` now returns an error instead of a bool, and `invalidCloneRefError` grew the symmetric `^/?et/` branch. All three of your repro refs now name the rule instead of echoing the shape:

```
/et/foo_bar/dogbark -> project "foo_bar" must be 3-32 characters of letters, digits and '-', not starting or ending with '-'
/et/paul/dog_bark   -> repo "dog_bark" must be 1-64 characters of letters, digits, '.' and '-', not starting or ending with '.' or '-', and with no consecutive dots
/et/paul            -> expected /et/<project>/<repo> or <project>/<repo> (2 names, got 1)
```

The messages name the offending segment, so they avoid the double-ref shape the `gh/` branch produces. A bare two-segment ref (`paul/.foo`) still gets the shape list — declaring a token is the whole test — and that boundary is now pinned by a test, since it's what protects #2223's `git@github.com:foo/bar` fix.

**Item 2 — tightened to the server.** I read `normalizeName` myself and your table is exact. Two extra confirmations: the repo lookup folds case too (`lower(repo_registry.name) = lower($2)` in `getRepoGroupByProjectAndFullName`), so accepting uppercase is right for both segments. Encoding the 3-char project minimum let me *delete* the hand-written `gh`/`et` forge-token guard — the rule it stood in for now does the work directly, so `ab/dogbark` is a local error as well. Consecutive dots are checked outside the regex (RE2 has no negative lookahead), and `dog--bark`/`dog-.bark` are pinned as *accepted*, because they're server-legal and a per-segment regex would refuse them.

**Item 3 — `.git`.** Not stripped or rejected at parse time, as you said. `noRepoNamedErr` became a typed error so the clone path recognises the miss via `errors.As` rather than its text (message unchanged). The passthrough branch gets the same advice as a hedged stderr note after `git clone` fails, only for an `/et/` path carrying the suffix.

Two things worth your attention in the PR body:

- **Your OpenAPI correction is in**, with one addition: pinning the rules in the spec can't be done here. `core.openapi.json` is the pristine upstream spec, refreshed by curl-ing the running server (`internal/coreapi/gen.go`), so a hand edit would be reverted by the next sync — it belongs in entiredb.
- **One claim of yours I had to soften.** The ULID short-circuit is safe in practice but not for the stated reason: the CLI's `looksLikeULID` accepts *any* 26 Crockford-base32 chars, while the server's `LooksLikeRawULID` also requires the first char in `0`-`7`. So `REDACTED` is a legal server repo name the CLI misreads as an ID — I verified both predicates. Tightening it is one line and can't reject a real ULID, but it's shared by every org/project/repo/grant ref, so I flagged it rather than widening this PR.

`mise run fmt && mise run lint` clean (0 issues, run after fmt), `mise run test:ci` exit 0 with zero FAIL lines — the two macOS failures you warned about didn't fire this run.

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

### Baseline: how much does `cli` package init actually cost?

| | |
|---|---|
| Whole-binary init | **7.24 ms** median, 331 packages |
| `cmd/entire/cli` package init, `main` | **68.0 µs** |
| `cmd/entire/cli` package init, `HEAD` | **83.0 µs** |
| **Diff's marginal init cost** | **+15.0 µs** (microbenchmark independently predicted +15.8 µs) |

For scale, `chroma/v2/lexers` + `chroma/v2/styles` cost **5.9 ms** — 57% of all init, and ~390x the entire diff. The concern is legitimate in *kind* (`hooks` is registered in this same package at `root.go:208`, so all 22 regexes compile on every git-hook invocation), but 15 µs against the ~3 s hook p50 floor documented in CLAUDE.md is 0.0005%. Even at 1,000 hook invocations per session that is 15 ms total, once.

### Finding 1 (informational — recommend no change): the cost is in the *tightened* regexes, not the new ones

`cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go:92-93, 190, 213`. The premise that the newly-added package-level regex is the expense is backwards. Bounded repetition expands in `regexp/syntax`, so tightening `+` into `{0,62}` is far more expensive than adding a whole new pattern:

| regex | instructions | compile Δ | share of the +15 µs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nativeRepoRe` `{0,62}` (line 93) | 6 → **131** | +8.0 µs | **53%** |
| `nativeProjectRe` `{1,30}` (line 92) | 6 → **65** | +4.4 µs | **28%** |
| `nativeCloneURLGitSuffixRe` (new, line 190) | 28 | +2.8 µs | 17% |
| `nativeCloneRefPrefixRe` (new, line 213) | 8 | +0.6 µs | 4% |

So **81% of the added init cost is the two tightenings** and only 19% is the two new regexes — `{0,62}` alone costs more than both additions combined, because it expands to 131 instructions where `[A-Za-z0-9.-]+` needed 6.

A cheaper spelling exists: keep `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.-]*[A-Za-z0-9]?$` (~8 instructions) and move the bounds to `len(repo) > 64`. That recovers ~12 of the 15 µs and arguably reads better, since `3-32` in the rule string would then match a literal `len` check instead of a `{1,30}` the reader must add two to. **But at this magnitude there is no performance case for the churn**, and the current form keeps one rule in one place. Leave it.

Likewise the two trivial new regexes: `^/?et/` is expressible as `strings.HasPrefix(ref, "et/") || strings.HasPrefix(ref, "/et/")` (0 compile, 2.6 ns vs 39 ns per match). Done. Four reviews ran in parallel; I applied six findings and skipped three, then re-ran the full gate (`fmt` → `lint` 0 issues → `test:ci` exit 0, zero FAIL lines). Net **−57 lines**, pushed to PR #2240 as a second commit, and the PR body corrected where it described something I removed.

## Fixed

**One real altitude problem — the passthrough `.git` note is gone.** It fired on *any* non-zero exit from `git clone`, so it appended "if the repo was not found, retry without it" to `destination path already exists`, to auth failures, and to network failures. It had to hedge precisely because at that layer it can't see why git failed. I verified the reviewer's claim: `git-remote-entire`'s `fatalMessage` (`cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:244`) already holds both the parsed URL and the classified transfer error, already rewrites the typed URL for the wrong-cluster case, and covers plain `git clone entire://…` and `git fetch` too — not just `entire repo clone <full URL>`. Mine was the shallow copy of it. `gitDirSuffix` now records why there's no hint there, and it's filed as the follow-up (it needs the not-found error classified at that layer, so it isn't a drop-in). **This is the one thing I subtracted** — your handoff said the passthrough case was "worth considering", and having considered it, it belongs one layer down. Say the word if you'd rather have the hedged version back in the meantime. The lookup-miss hint, which fires only where the suffix is provably the cause, is untouched.

**`noRepoNamedError` → `errNoRepoNamed` sentinel.** Two reviewers independently caught that my doc comment claimed a benefit the code didn't take: the one consumer never reads the name off the type, it takes it from its own parameter and uses `errors.As` purely to classify. 9 lines → 3, message byte-identical, and it restores symmetry with `noOrgNamedErr`/`noProjectNamedErr` directly above it.

**Two prefix regexes → one `declaresForge` predicate.** Both tested for a fixed literal token with no alternation, class, or capture. Also gave the `gh` path token the constant its native counterpart already had, so the two call sites read alike.

**Inlined the two single-use rule strings** at the `fmt.Errorf` that prints them (no `lll` linter, and this also resolved a reviewer's separate complaint that the doc bullets and the constants had already drifted typographically), and **folded the miss fixture into `serveNativeRepo`** — a nil repo serves the lookup miss, instead of restating 22 of its 25 lines.

Description:
Problem:
When a user types an invalid repo clone reference, the error message sometimes lists every possible format instead of telling them which specific rule they broke. For instance, someone typing /et/ab/cd (a 2-character project) should see "projects must be 3+ characters," not a generic menu of all acceptable shapes.
Solution:
The code now tracks parsing errors separately for each clone reference format (native /et/, mirror /gh/, and full entire:// URLs). When a reference begins with a forge token (/et/ or /gh/), the parser's specific error message—explaining exactly which rule was violated—is returned instead of the generic shape list. For references that don't declare a token (like bare paul/.foo), the shape list is shown since both parsers failed only because the ref didn't match their grammar.
Native reference validation was also strengthened to match the actual server rules from entiredb: projects must be 3–32 characters with hyphens only in the middle, repos 1–64 with dots/hyphens only in the middle and no consecutive dots. Error messages now explain exactly which constraint was violated. A separate mechanism detects .git suffixes on repo lookups and suggests dropping them, since .git is a legal repo name and cannot be stripped at parse time. The documentation was updated to explain these rules and their purpose in detail.

Pull request overview This PR improves `entire repo clone`’s handling of Entire-native `/et//` refs by (1) validating native refs against the server’s actual name *shape* (not just charset) and (2) ensuring `/et/`-prefixed parse failures preserve the native parser’s specific reason (mirroring existing `/gh/` behavior). It also adds targeted user guidance for the ambiguous “native ref with `.git` suffix” scenario without stripping the suffix at parse time. **Changes:** - Tighten native ref parsing to match server-enforced project/repo name constraints (length, edge `-`/`.`, and `..` prohibition) and return specific native parse errors when the ref declares `et/`. - Introduce a typed repo-miss error (`noRepoNamedError`) so callers can detect “repo name not found” via `errors.As` and attach `.git`-suffix retry hints only when the suffix is provably the cause. - Expand unit test coverage for native ref edge cases, `/et/` error reporting behavior, and `.git`-suffix hinting (including passthrough `entire://` URLs).

Read it properly this time. My earlier report came from the inline-comments endpoint only — the command I ran for the review body matched on `copilot-pull-request-reviewer` when the actual login is `copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]`, so it returned empty and I summarized without it. Here's the full picture.

## The review body

Verdict "🟢 Approval recommended", with its own metadata saying **Comments generated: 1** and **Review effort level: Lite**. So the single inline finding I already fixed is the whole of it — no second finding hiding in the collapsed sections. The rest is a summary, a per-file table, and a footer suggesting a `code-review` agent skill or MCP servers for "context-aware, tailored reviews".

## The finding itself — valid, already fixed

`repo_clone.go:134`, `resolveNativeCloneURL`'s doc comment claiming the URL carries "no .git suffix — a /et/ path with it would 404". Correct catch: that conflates the two cases this PR separates. The URL is `repoRemoteURL`'s output, the server's own path, so it ends in `.git` exactly when the repo is genuinely named that — and then it resolves fine. Fixed in `caea539da`.

## The part that matters more: the review is stale

Submitted **09:34:13Z** against `0834e8c6b` (`original_commit_id` confirms it) — four minutes after my first commit, and **73 minutes before** the cleanup commit `266518775`. Copilot has not looked at the branch since. Its overview describes two mechanisms that no longer exist:

- "Introduce a typed repo-miss error (`noRepoNamedError`) so callers can detect ... via `errors.As`" — replaced by the `errNoRepoNamed` sentinel and `errors.Is`.
- "`.git`-suffix hinting (**including passthrough `entire://` URLs**)" / "adds `.git`-suffix hint/note behavior" — that passthrough note is the thing I deleted as wrong-layer.

So "Approval recommended" is a Lite-effort verdict on a superseded commit, and the file-summary table now misdescribes the branch. I'd not read it as a signal on the current head. Notably, the two things it praised are the two the parallel cleanup review argued out of the diff — which is a reasonable illustration of what "Lite" buys.

Thread state: **unresolved and not outdated** (`position` still maps into the current diff, so GitHub re-anchored it onto my corrected comment rather than marking it obsolete), and `reviewDecision=REVIEW_REQUIRED` — consistent with the approvals gate being the only blocker.

Two things I can do, neither of which I've done since you asked me to look rather than act:

- **Re-request Copilot's review** so its verdict covers the final three commits instead of the first.
- **Reply on the thread and resolve it**, saying what changed in `caea539da`.

content.text:
**No.** My change covers exactly one entry point — `entire repo clone`'s ref argument. Here's the actual map, verified rather than assumed.

## Where each of the three mechanisms stops

**Name-shape validation is clone-only, and that's defensible.** It's the CLI's only client-side copy of the server's name rules. `repo get/delete/visibility` and `grant repo add/list/remove` all resolve through `resolveRepoRef`, which does ULID-or-name with no shape check — so `entire repo get ".." --project paul` still costs a round trip. Unlike clone, though, those commands need the network anyway, so nothing is wasted the way it was for clone. `repo create`/`project create` send names unvalidated and let the server reject, which is right for a write path. I'd leave all of this alone.

**The forge-token reason dispatch is genuinely clone-local.** Nothing else has two competing ref grammars to pick between.

## The one that isn't covered — and it's a live bug

**`.git` is now answered five ways, and mine is the outlier.** These all strip unconditionally, for *every* forge:

| site | strips for |
| --- | --- |
| `gitremote/gitremote.go:247` (`splitOwnerRepo`) | every forge, incl. `et/` |
| `gitremote/gitremote.go:154` (SCP path) | every forge |
| `trail_cmd.go:2296` (`parseTrailRepoArg`) | every forge |
| `experts_cmd.go:391` (`parseExpertsRepo`) | every forge |
| `repo_mirror.go:1321` (`parseMirrorCloneURL`) | GitHub only (fine) |

For GitHub that's harmless — GitHub disallows names ending in `.git`. For **native** repos, where `foo.git` is legal (the entire premise of my item 3), it's wrong. The concrete bite: clone a repo genuinely named `dogbark.git`, and `ResolveRemoteRepo` reads its own configured remote back as `dogbark` — and that flows into **8 call sites across 6 files** (trail, api, experts, recap, explain, entireapi_client). So most repo-scoped commands would silently target the wrong name for that repo.

That also means my PR body undercounts: I wrote "three different answers" and named only `splitOwnerRepo`. It's five. Worth correcting — say the word and I'll fix the body.

**Bonus gap found while checking: native refs are rejected where they look supported.** `IsSupportedForge` only knows `gh` (`hostToForge` has one entry), despite gitremote's own doc comment saying the forge id is `"gh"`, `"et"`, …. Against the built binary:

```
$ entire trail list --repo et/paul/dogbark
invalid --repo "et/paul/dogbark": "et" is not a supported forge id
(use a forge id like "gh", or pass a clone URL such as https://github.com/paul/dogbark)
```

Native repos can't be addressed by `trail --repo` in the bare form at all, and the error points at a **github.com URL for a native repo**. The URL form (`--repo entire://host/et/p/r`) works, because `ParseURL` reads the forge off the path and bypasses that map.

## What is consistent

`explain --repo` deliberately normalizes to `gh/` and reuses `parseMirrorCloneRef`, so it shares the GitHub charset validation — GitHub-only by design. `search --repo` accepts `et/proj/repo` but only string-matches it against the fetched repo index, so there's nothing to validate and an unmatchable filter fails locally.

## What I'd do

One shared, forge-aware decision on `.git`: strip for `gh`, never for `et`, behind a single helper used by `splitOwnerRepo` and the three ref parsers. That's a separate PR touching `gitremote` plus four call sites, and it changes behavior for anyone whose native remote ends in `.git` — so it's your call, not something I'd fold into #2240. The `IsSupportedForge` gap is a second, smaller one (add `et`, and fix that error's suggestion).

Want me to open either of those, or just file them as issues?

content.text:
**Yes** — and it genuinely works server-side, which is the part I'd only inferred before. Verified against entiredb @ `2b81a3557`:

**Creation passes.** `NormalizeRepoName("test.git")` clears every rule: 8 chars (1–64), starts and ends alphanumeric so no edge `-`/`.`, the dot is interior, no `..`, not a raw ULID, all lowercase. Repos are also *not* checked against `reserved_names.txt` — that gate is `isReservedProjectName`, called only from `CreateProject`.

**The URL keeps the suffix.** `core/coreapi/repos.go:161` stamps `url := "/et/" + project.Name + "/" + name` verbatim, so the row is `/et/<project>/test.git`.

**Serving resolves it.** `handleRepo` looks up `CanonicaliseMirrorPath(CanonicalizeRepoURL(path))`, and `CanonicaliseMirrorPath` returns anything without the `/gh/` prefix **unchanged** — so a `/et/` path keeps its `.git` and matches the stamped row. The token-exchange side agrees: `ClassifyAudience` takes the `/et/` branch and keeps `u.Path` as-is. So `git clone entire://host/et/<project>/test.git` resolves, and `…/test` does not — exactly what the new hint tells you.

The one place that *does* reject a `.git` suffix, `validateMirrorRepoURL` ("url must not carry a .git suffix"), requires the `/gh/` prefix, so it never sees native repos. That asymmetry is deliberate: GitHub disallows `.git`-suffixed names upstream, so mirrors can safely canonicalise; native names can't.

One creation caveat: it must be lowercase. `Test.git` is refused at create — only *lookups* fold case.

## But you'd walk straight into the CLI bug

After cloning, your remote is `entire://host/et/proj/test.git`, and `gitremote.ParseURL` routes it through `splitOwnerRepo`, which strips `.git` unconditionally:

```
entire://host/et/proj/test.git
  → splitForgePrefix → forge="et", path="proj/test.git"
  → splitOwnerRepo   → TrimSuffix(".git") → owner="proj", repo="test"
```

So the CLI reads its own remote back as `test`, and every command resolving the repo off the remote — the 8 `ResolveRemoteRepo` call sites in trail, api, experts, recap, explain, entireapi_client — would target `et/proj/test`, which doesn't exist. `entire repo clone` itself is the only path that gets it right, because that's the one I just fixed.

So: the server supports `test.git` end-to-end; the CLI does not, yet. Which is a decent argument for landing the forge-aware strip *before* anyone creates one — right now the failure would look like "Entire can't see my repo" with nothing pointing at the name. Want me to open that one?

content.text: No — dots are fine on GitHub. This repo's own code depends on that:

input.command: sed -n '30,80p' cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror_probe.go

content.text:
No — dots are perfectly legal in GitHub repo names. The code here is built on that:

```go
gitHubOwnerPat = `([A-Za-z0-9-]+)`     // owners: no dots
gitHubRepoPat  = `([A-Za-z0-9._-]+?)`  // repos: dots and underscores allowed
```

with the comment stating it plainly: *"GitHub owners are `[A-Za-z0-9-]` and repos are `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`"*. And `gitHubDotOnlyRe` exists precisely because dots are otherwise allowed — it's a narrow guard against a name that is *nothing but* dots (`.`, `..`), which would embed a literal `..` in the `/gh/` path and the token audience. If dots were banned outright, that regex would have no reason to exist.

Real examples: `socket.io`, `next.js`, `docs.rs`, and `.github` — which not only contains a dot but *starts* with one.

So the actual GitHub rules are narrower than "no dots":

- **Allowed:** alphanumerics, `-`, `_`, `.`. Other characters (spaces included) get silently replaced with `-`.
- **Rejected:** a name that is only dots, and a name **ending in `.git`**.

That last one is the only claim I made, and it's the one the code leans on. It's why the asymmetry in the previous answer holds: stripping a trailing `.git` from a `/gh/` path is safe because no GitHub repo can be named `foo.git`, while stripping it from an `/et/` path is wrong because a native repo can. Dots *elsewhere* are fine on both sides — `entire-trails.el` mirrors from GitHub and is a legal native name, which is why it's the example used throughout the doc comments.

Where the two do differ is the owner/project half and the edges:

| | GitHub repo | Entire native repo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| interior dot | yes | yes |
| leading/trailing dot | yes (`.github`) | **no** |
| consecutive dots | yes (`a..b` is accepted) | **no** |
| underscore | yes | **no** |
| ends in `.git` | **no** | yes |

So Entire's native rules are stricter on dots than GitHub's in three of those rows, and looser in exactly one — the `.git` ending. That's the pairing that makes a single unconditional strip in the CLI wrong.

content.text:
Done — pushed as `3c3d6c1f4`, PR body's item 3 rewritten to describe the reversal rather than the old policy. `mise run fmt && lint` clean, `test:ci` exit 0 with zero failures.

## What changed

**Both clone-ref parsers now trim the suffix before validating the name**, and the ordering is load-bearing in each: `.git` alone fails as an *empty* name rather than sneaking through as a dotted one, and `/gh/<owner>/..git` — which isn't dot-only as typed — becomes so once the suffix goes, so the existing dot-only guard catches it.

**The mirror side gets this for the first time.** This turned out to be a pre-existing bug I hadn't noticed until I tested it: `/gh/foo/bar.git` used to look up a repo GitHub cannot have, then tell you to onboard it as `entire repo mirror create github.com/foo/bar.git` — an impossible name. Now:

```
/gh/foo/bar.git  -> no mirror found for /gh/foo/bar; run 'entire repo mirror create github.com/foo/bar' to onboard it
/gh/foo/..git    -> invalid <repo>: repo cannot be dot-only
/gh/foo/.git     -> invalid <repo>: repo name is empty once the .git suffix is dropped
```

`parseGitHubURL` already accepted `(?:\.git)?` on the URL forms, so the `/gh/` shorthand was the odd one out.

**`repo create` now refuses a name ending in `.git`**, suggesting the trimmed form. This is the piece that makes the policy coherent rather than just lenient — the server *would* accept `web.git`, so without it the CLI could mint a repo it can then only address by ULID.

**The hint machinery is gone**, and with it the `errNoRepoNamed` sentinel that existed only to key it — `resolveref.go` is now byte-identical to `main` (verified: `git diff main -- resolveref.go` is empty). The `serveNativeRepo` fixture went back to its value signature too, since the nil-miss branch lost its only callers.

## The tradeoff, stated plainly

This is a deliberate client-side narrowing of what the server allows, not a claim the server agrees. I re-verified that the server really does keep the suffix on native paths — `CanonicaliseMirrorPath` passes non-`/gh/` paths through untouched, and `repos.go:161` stamps `/et/<project>/<name>` verbatim. So a native repo named `foo.git` remains creatable via the API or web, and is now unaddressable *by name* in the CLI. Escape hatches: its ULID, and a full `entire://` URL, which `clone` still forwards to git verbatim.

The upside is that the five-way inconsistency I reported earlier is now closed by *joining* the majority rather than by touching `gitremote`, `trail_cmd` and `experts_cmd` — `repo clone` was the sole holdout, so nothing else needed changing.

Still open and untouched: `IsSupportedForge` doesn't know `et`, so `trail --repo et/paul/dogbark` is rejected outright with a suggestion pointing at a github.com URL. That's noted in the PR body as a separate gap — happy to fix it next if you want it in this PR or its own.

content.text:
Done — `a3d820a70`, PR body updated with it as item 4. Full `test:ci` green, lint 0 issues.

**Investigating it changed the fix.** The gap wasn't "the CLI wrongly rejects a valid forge" — it was two bugs sharing one wrong error message.

`IsSupportedForge` was backed by `forgeToHost`, a map of **upstream** git hosts to their ids. A native repo has no upstream host, so `et` was simply absent — and the two questions *"does this forge have a public host?"* and *"is this a forge token in an `entire://` path?"* had silently collapsed into one. `gitremote.pathForges` now owns `{gh, et}` separately, plus the placeholder spelling of the segments that follow, since a mirror is addressed by owner and a native repo by project. `forgeToHost` is untouched, so `CanonicalHost` still falls back to the cluster host for a native remote rather than inventing a forge host — pinned by a test, because that's the thing a careless widening would break.

That fixed a second bug I hadn't reported: `git clone entire://et/paul/dogbark` was dying on `lookup et: no such host`, because the forge-id-in-the-host-slot check didn't recognize `et`. It now gets the same actionable message `gh` always got, with correct labels:

```
fatal: entire:// URL is missing its cluster host ("et" is a forge id, not a host).
The full form is entire://<cluster-host>/et/<project>/<repo>.
To clone it, run:

    entire repo clone /et/paul/dogbark
```

**But trails still refuse native refs — deliberately.** I checked entire-api before widening, and it's the decisive constraint: `validTrailsHosts` admits `{gh, et}`, but `resolvableTrailsHosts` is `{gh}` alone, with an explicit comment that `full_name` rows carry no forge host so *"et fails closed into the collapsed 404 … extend resolution deliberately then, don't widen this set."*

So accepting `et` would have traded a clear local error for an opaque server 404 — indistinguishable from permission-denied, by design. Instead the rejection stays and tells the truth:

```
invalid --repo "et/paul/dogbark": trails are not available for Entire-native repos yet;
pass a GitHub mirror as gh/<owner>/<repo> or a github.com clone URL
```

It now also catches the **URL** spelling (`--repo entire://host/et/p/r`), which previously slipped past the forge check straight into that 404 — a third thing that was broken and unreported.

One judgment call worth your eye: that check encodes client-side knowledge of a server-side gate, the same maintenance trap I flagged for the name rules. I've commented it to come out when entire-api gains forge-scoped naming, and documented the pairing in CLAUDE.md, but it will go stale silently if nobody looks. The alternative — let it through and eat the 404 — is honest but useless to the user, so I picked the informative one and flagged it.

Also: `missingClusterHostMessage` lost its "To pick a mirror interactively" line in favour of a neutral "To clone it, run:". The old wording was accurate for `gh` and wrong for `et`, and `repo clone` explains the picker itself when it prompts. Say the word if you'd rather keep the per-forge phrasing.
